notes: Within each sequence both products use the same main dependency lockfile and identical recovery_paths harness; the delivered-runtime sequence has 43 cases. Only benchmark instrumentation is copied into the frozen baseline.

No competing Cargo builds or benchmarks ran during each sequence. Desktop scheduling and hardware resources were not reserved; drift-failing cases cannot establish candidate latency or throughput claims.
Every invocation performs untimed poison/presence/content preflights. Option<Vec> recovery drops and reallocates missing buffers inside its measured closure; ShardSlot cases reuse backing buffers.

Allocation bytes are cumulative requested allocation sizes for one warm operation, not peak or retained memory. The repeated-observation flag requires matching allocation counts and bytes in both A stages and both B stages.
The initial and compacted drafts were superseded before push; their observations remain diagnostic only and cannot describe the delivered runtime.
The final no-op recovery path validates all present lengths and skips plan preparation. It was added after the compacted draft identified unnecessary empty-plan work.

Frozen baseline git metadata is unknown because it is an archive; the explicit baseline revision above identifies product source. Dirty final runtime metadata reflects benchmark/docs/test-only edits, not additional production code.

Only per-case final-runtime comparisons passing both 5% drift gates may be discussed as local latency observations. No overall or downstream RustFS throughput, x86 runtime, or browser integration claim is made.
